sentences.text: Hesperogavialis was an extinct genus belonging to the gryposuchine subfamily of gavialids, a group of crocodilians known for their long, narrow snouts.
The posterior portion of the Hesperogavialis skull is unknown, making its classification within the family more difficult than for other gavialoids.
The type species, H. cruxenti, was found in the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela.
A third species has been recognized from the Solimões Formation in Acre, but it has not yet been formally named.
The genus Hesperogavialis was described by Bocquetin and Buffetaut in 1981.
The name H. bocquentini was proposed by Sousa-Filho in 1999 but is considered a nomen nudum.
Hesperogavialis is classified within the family Gavialidae.
Hesperogavialis belongs to the subfamily Gryposuchinae.
Fossils of Hesperogavialis have been found in Venezuela and Brazil and date from the Middle to Late Miocene.
Hesperogavialis lived between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago during the Tortonian to Messinian stages.
It is debated whether Hesperogavialis is more closely related to the extant Asian Gavialis than to other South American gryposuchines.
Researchers suggest that the relationship between Hesperogavialis and Asian Gavialis implies multiple dispersal events from the Old World to South America.
Some researchers propose that the traits linking Hesperogavialis to Asian gavialoids are independently derived characteristics unique to the genus.
